summary: Polk County, OR lookout site on ODF land: 1948 24-ft live-in tower or 1954 house (sources disagree); removed or destroyed 1967 or dismantled after 1969. Now gone.

facts.design: enclosed wooden live-in tower, 24 ft (register); three-story enclosed lookout house per Oregon Lookouts
facts.status_note: Register says removed in 1967 and firelookout.com says destroyed in 1967; Oregon Lookouts dates the decision to dismantle to 1969. No source describes the site today.

staffing.status: in disuse for several years before 1969

events.note: 24-foot enclosed wooden live-in tower constructed (register and firelookout.com; Oregon Lookouts gives 1954 for a different house)
Three-story enclosed lookout house constructed (Oregon Lookouts only; conflicts with the 1948 tower)
Register says removed; firelookout.com says destroyed
After several years of disuse, wind damage, vandalism and repair costs, the decision was made to dismantle the lookout (Oregon Lookouts)

evidence.supports: 24-foot enclosed wooden live-in tower built 1948, removed 1967
evidence.quote: In 1948, a 24' enclosed wooden live-in tower was constructed, which was removed in 1967.

evidence.supports: administered by the Oregon Department of Forestry
administered by the Oregon Department of Forestry
listed among former fire lookout sites

evidence.quote: A 500 gallon water tank was constructed at Condenser Peak.
1954: A three story enclosed lookout house constructed.

evidence.supports: disuse for several years, wind damage, vandalism and repair costs, decision to dismantle in 1969
evidence.quote: 1969: After several years of disuse, wind damage, vandalism and the expense of repairs the decision was made to dismantle the lookout structure.

resolved_conflicts.field: first tower or house, and its date
resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register and firelookout.com give a 24-foot live-in tower built in 1948. Oregon Lookouts gives a 500-gallon water tank in 1950 and a three-story enclosed house in 1954. Not reconciled; the story reports both.
Register and firelookout.com date removal or destruction to 1967; Oregon Lookouts dates the decision to dismantle to 1969. Not reconciled; the story says the year is uncertain.

sources.title: Condenser Peak Lookout Site
sources.publisher: Former Fire Lookout Sites Register, Forest Fire Lookout Association

notes_for_editor: Location, elevation, agency and gone status agree across sources; the construction and removal dates do not, and the story reports both versions. No height_m set: the 24-foot figure comes from the register and firelookout.com, but Oregon Lookouts describes a different three-story house. Brief record had no design or height to correct; elevation 890.0 m matches the register. Oregon Lookouts cites the Corvallis Gazette-Times for the 1950 tank; that clipping was not opened. Access and current condition unknown.
